annotations.description: Playing Mountain instead of Arid Mesa on turn 1 is suboptimal. Arid Mesa is a fetch land that can find a Mountain, and playing it first preserves flexibility. With Ruby Medallion in hand (wanting to cast it turn 2), playing Arid Mesa now and cracking it later (or immediately) thins the deck. More importantly, if the opponent plays something like Orcish Bowmasters, having the fetch uncracked gives you the option to fetch at instant speed in response. Playing the basic Mountain first means you'll play Arid Mesa on a later turn when you might prefer to play Commercial District or Castle Locthwain instead. Fetch lands are generally better to play early to maximize deck thinning and sequencing flexibility.
annotations.actionTaken: Played basic Mountain as the turn 1 land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Arid Mesa, keeping the option to crack it at the optimal time. On turn 2, play Mountain and cast Ruby Medallion. This preserves maximum flexibility and gets deck thinning earlier.

annotations.description: With two Castle Locthwains and two Swamps in hand, playing Castle Locthwain first is slightly suboptimal. Since Castle Locthwain enters tapped unless you control a Swamp, playing it turn 1 means it enters tapped and you have no mana available this turn. Playing a Swamp first would give you 1 black mana available on turn 1 (relevant for potential plays), and then playing Castle Locthwain on turn 2 alongside the second Swamp would let it enter untapped since you'd already control a Swamp. By leading with Castle Locthwain, you guarantee it enters tapped, and on turn 2 you'll play a Swamp (untapped), giving you only 2 mana. If you had led Swamp turn 1, then Castle Locthwain turn 2 enters untapped, also giving you 2 mana on turn 2 — the same. However, the key difference is that leading Swamp gives you 1 mana on turn 1 for potential instant-speed plays (like holding up for Orcish Bowmasters on opponent's turn 1 — though that costs 1B so you'd need 2 mana). Actually, with only 1 land either way on turn 1, you can't cast Bowmasters. But the principle of playing basics before conditional lands is correct sequencing — leading Swamp ensures Castle Locthwain enters untapped on turn 2, preserving future flexibility and tempo.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Castle Locthwain as the turn 1 land drop, which enters tapped (no Swamp in play).
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp on turn 1 to have an untapped land, then play Castle Locthwain on turn 2 where it enters untapped thanks to already controlling a Swamp.

annotations.description: Against a Storm deck (evidenced by Desperate Ritual, Pyretic Ritual, Grapeshot, Ruby Medallion in the format), Emperor of Bones is a slow value creature that doesn't interact with the opponent's game plan. Orcish Bowmasters would be better held for the opponent's turn (it has flash) to potentially punish card draw from Wrenn's Resolve or similar effects. However, the bigger issue is that playing Emperor of Bones on turn 2 is a proactive play that doesn't pressure or disrupt a combo opponent. Holding up Orcish Bowmasters (flash) or Sheoldred's Edict mana would be more appropriate against a combo deck, keeping interaction available. That said, Emperor of Bones does apply some pressure and the opponent hasn't revealed their full game plan yet, so this is a minor sequencing/strategic error rather than a major one.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Emperor of Bones on turn 2
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn holding up 2 mana for Orcish Bowmasters (flash) to potentially punish the opponent's card draw spells like Wrenn's Resolve, or hold Sheoldred's Edict. Playing Emperor of Bones is not terrible but leaving up flash interaction is generally better against combo strategies.

annotations.description: Playing Commercial District (which enters tapped) instead of Mountain wastes mana this turn. With Ruby Medallion costing 2 (reduced from nothing since it's an artifact, not red — wait, Ruby Medallion is an artifact so it costs {2}), and the hand containing Pyretic Ritual and Desperate Ritual for mana generation, having an untapped land matters. Playing Mountain would give 3 available mana (2 lands + ritual potential), enabling Ruby Medallion this turn and potentially setting up a bigger storm turn. Commercial District entering tapped means only 2 mana available from lands this turn. With Mountain, you could play Ruby Medallion (2 mana from Mountain + existing Mountain), then on future turns benefit from the cost reduction. Playing the tapped land delays the game plan by a turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Commercial District (enters tapped) as the land for turn 3.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain untapped, then cast Ruby Medallion with 2 available mana. This develops the key cost-reduction artifact on curve and allows Commercial District to be played on a later turn when the tempo loss matters less. The storm deck wants to maximize mana efficiency to combo as early as possible.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones exiles a card from a graveyard, and if it later gets +1/+1 counters (via Adapt), it can reanimate a creature card exiled with it. Grapeshot is a sorcery, not a creature, so it can never be reanimated by Emperor of Bones' ability. The opponent's graveyard contains only non-creature spells, so none are ideal targets, but exiling a ritual (Pyretic Ritual or Desperate Ritual) would at least deny the Storm opponent potential recursion fuel or Past in Flames value, which is more strategically relevant than exiling Grapeshot (which already resolved and whose storm copies don't go to the graveyard). Exiling a ritual is marginally better as graveyard hate against a Storm deck.

annotations.betterLine: Exile Desperate Ritual or Pyretic Ritual instead, since these are the key mana enablers for the Storm deck and denying them from potential graveyard recursion (e.g., Past in Flames) is more impactful. None of these are creatures so none can be reanimated by Emperor of Bones regardless.
